growth_story.headline: Income per person in São Tomé and Príncipe is about where it was in 1979: a boom on oil hopes and aid faded after 2008, and power cuts now weigh on it.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in São Tomé and Príncipe fell by 0.5 percent a year from 1990 to 2000, a decade the sources say little about. From 2001 to 2008 it grew 3.0 percent a year, peaking at 6.2 percent in 2006, as market reforms, foreign aid and hopes of oil drew in private investment and lifted banking and services. From 2009 to 2025 growth slowed to 0.7 percent a year, after foreign investment, tourism earnings and aid fell with the global financial crisis and the expected oil bonuses did not fully arrive. The last decade averaged 0.5 percent a year, down from 1.8 in the decade before, and income per person has fallen every year since 2021 amid power cuts and costly fuel. It is now 6.5 percent below its 1979 peak.

threads.title: Reforms, oil hopes and aid
threads.text: From 2000 to 2003 the country lifted price controls, opened trade and sold state firms. The prospect of oil then lifted private investment, banking and services, while foreign aid paid for public investment. Income per person grew 3.0 percent a year from 2001 to 2008.

threads.title: Outside money dries up
threads.text: After 2008, foreign investment, tourism earnings and aid all fell at once, and oil signing bonuses fell short of hopes. The sources date the long slowdown to the global financial crisis. Income per person grew only 0.7 percent a year from 2009 to 2025.

threads.title: An aid-financed model fades
threads.text: Growth has long leaned on public investment paid for from abroad, and that aid has been shrinking. Investment fell from 25.5 percent of GDP in 2010 to 6.1 in 2023, before edging up to 8.7 in 2025.

citations.title: Sao Tome and Principe Economic Update, 1st Edition: Reforming State-Owned Enterprises for Higher Private Sector-Led Growth and Job Creation
citations.quote: São Tomé and Príncipe’s growth model, driven by externally financed public investment, is challenged by the decline in official development assistance inflows

threads.title: Power cuts and fuel costs
threads.text: The state power company runs costly diesel plants and owes large sums to the fuel supplier. In 2023 a fuel import crunch brought fuel shortages and severe power cuts. The crisis deepened in 2025, with outages hitting farms and services.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: São Tomé and Príncipe

threads.title: Young people leaving
threads.text: Too few jobs are being created for a young population, and many young people look for work abroad. The World Bank links this emigration to a shrinking pool of workers.

since_last_year.text: Over the past year the power crisis deepened, and in early 2026 the war in the Middle East pushed up the cost of imported fuel. The IMF cut its growth estimates for 2025 and 2026. Income per person fell 1.0 percent in 2025, the fifth straight year of decline.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe output that kept growing at a fair pace for much of the period, even after the 2008 slowdown. Income per person grew far less: 3.0 percent a year in 2001 to 2008 and 0.7 in 2009 to 2025, partly because the population kept growing. The gap shows again in 2025, when the sources report small output growth but income per person fell 1.0 percent.
